correctness.rationale: The known Gaussian-beta representation is reproduced with a precise normalization and dimensionless variance. The Kummer equation yields a Riccati identity forcing every level-half crossing upward when 0<a<1; verified beta-integral small- and large-argument expansions supply opposite endpoint signs and therefore exactly one root. Monotone likelihood ratio in the beta-shape parameter orders critical roots and gives endpoints. A proved sign-variation lemma bounds global derivative sign changes, precluding secondary peak pairs. At the unique crossing the heat equation makes the fourth derivative strictly negative. The analytic implicit-function theorem for P_x/x as a function of x² yields m²=3(tc-t)+O((tc-t)²). All normalization and endpoint cases a=1 and a>1 are treated separately. The original standalone numerical checker passed five threshold roots, five quartic signs, ten off-critical sign checks, ten mode scans and four peak-onset tests; these finite checks are corroboration only.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The models and formulas in the first three references are mathematically equivalent to the stationary setup, so overlap is conceded. Those sources do not state a proof that the root is globally unique and strictly monotone for the entire 0<a<1 family, nor the exact dimensionless square-root amplitude sqrt(3). A change of names or parameters cannot make their known formulas new; the claim is confined to the mathematical global/critical refinements.

evidence: No exact published table of the universal sqrt(3) peak-splitting amplitude was found in the checked source equations or phase diagrams. Published boundary points already belong to the cited 2024 study and are not re-claimed.
The 2024 arXiv article already contains a numerical thermal phase diagram and tabulated an example boundary point; those numerical points do not imply the universal exact onset asymptotic.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Records and published figures were compared for implication rather than string identity. The absence of a matching result is limited evidence, never proof of uniqueness or priority; the 2024 and 2026 equivalent physical models are incorporated as closest prior art.

originality.rationale: The published 2024 and 2026 sources already state the exact Gaussian-convolved beta law, central-curvature equation, and qualitative two-phase picture; these are expressly not claimed. The surviving result proves (i) each persistence parameter below one has exactly one transverse thermal branch, (ii) strict monotonicity and endpoint limits of that branch, (iii) global exclusion of additional modality branches, and (iv) a universal exact peak-splitting constant from the heat equation. The inspected sources give phase plots and local criteria but not these combined global assertions or the universal onset coefficient. Semantic mathematical-record queries yielded no competing matched statement. Possible coverage by general scale-space theory remains a documented, nondecisive risk.
residual_risks: Gaussian scale-space/total positivity theory may contain a general theorem implying mode restriction and square-root pitchfork amplitude; the applied one-dimensional beta-family parameter-order proof was not located in the inspected sources.

The 2024 and 2026 papers explicitly know the phase curve and some qualitative modalities; a stronger derivation outside the inspected passages, or equivalent statements in older theses, could narrow or subsume the surviving contribution.
Semantic record retrieval cannot prove global novelty, and independent scientific audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: For the physically meaningful phase transition in a standard active-matter model, the literature provides a mode-threshold equation and plots but no certified full monotonicity/no-hidden-branches characterization. The result establishes a complete, robust thermal-mode phase diagram for every persistence ratio in the one-dimensional model, identifies the degeneracy order at its boundary, and determines a nontrivial exact universal onset coefficient that permits quantitative predictions of peak separation as thermal noise approaches the transition. These are natural phase invariants; this is not an arbitrary parameter slice, a numerical fit, or a mere restatement of the known convolution.
